# Task: adapt (branch demo/adapt). SHOULD/STRETCH feature: must not threaten the main demo. Owns studio/adapt/ (new), studio/web/js/adapt/ (new), studio/web/css/adapt.css (new). Do not edit studio/server/app.py, studio/wiring.py, studio/policy/ or studio/web/index.html (owned by others). Allowed network: PyPI only.

Objective: show that the model adapts to a scientist's own domain: fine-tune the DQN edit policy on the user's logged manual edits, and measure honestly whether it now ranks their choices higher.

Build
1. `dataset.py`: `Transition` = the policy transition format `(parent_smiles, edit_id, site, child_smiles, reward)` (see `studio/policy/README.md` and the manual export format from `studio/server/manual.py` on `demo/api`; your input is just a list of such dicts, so you do not depend on that branch). Validate each step with RDKit and the registry (`studio.registry.get_registry()`); drop invalid steps and report how many were dropped.
2. `finetune.py`: start from the base policy (`studio.policy.policy.load_policy(op_ids)`; if it falls back to `UniformPolicy`, build a fresh `DQNPolicy` over the registry op ids; read `studio/policy/policy.py` and `features.py` first). Train an IMITATION objective on a COPY of the network: for each step, softmax cross-entropy over the scores of all applicable `(op, site)` candidates for the parent (`registry.applicable(parent)`), with the user's chosen edit as the target; small learning rate, <= 300 optimiser steps, hard wall-clock cap 60 s, deterministic seed. Refuse with a clear message when fewer than 5 valid steps exist.
3. `evaluate.py`: held-out top-1 / top-3 hit rate of the adapted policy vs the base policy vs uniform random, using an 80/20 split with a fixed seed; when there are fewer than 30 steps use leave-one-out cross-validation. Report n, the hit rates and a bootstrap 95% interval. Be explicit in the result payload (`note`) when n is small. Never tune until the number looks good; report what it is.
4. `store.py`: adapters saved under `$STUDIO_CACHE_DIR/adapters/<owner>/<adapter_id>.pt` with a JSON sidecar (owner, created_at, n_steps, op-id hash, base checkpoint name, hit rates). `policy_factory.py: load_adapted_policy(adapter_id, owner) -> Policy` (falls back to the base policy and says so if the file is missing or the op-id hash differs).
5. `jobs.py` + `install.py: install(app)`: ONE worker thread, queue length <= 3, per-job timeout 90 s, status/progress; routes under `/api/adapt`: `POST /jobs {transitions | manual_session_id}` -> `{job_id}`, `GET /jobs/{id}` (progress, result payload with the evaluation), `GET /adapters`, `DELETE /adapters/{id}`. Owner = the cookie `studio_sid` session (the `accounts` agent adds logins later; define `owner_of(request)` as a small function the integrator can swap). Request size caps (<= 2000 transitions).
6. `studio/web/js/adapt/adapt.js` (self-injecting ES module, dark theme): in manual mode (listen to the bus in `studio/web/README.md` and the `#panel-manual` mount), once >= 5 steps are logged, show an "Adapt to my edits" button -> progress -> a before/after bar chart (base vs adapted vs random hit rate, with n and the interval, and the honesty note) -> a "Use my adapted policy for new runs" toggle that dispatches `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("metis:adapter-selected", {detail: {adapter_id}}))` and sets `window.MetisStudio = window.MetisStudio || {}; window.MetisStudio.extraConfig = {adapter_id}` (the integrator wires this into run requests).
7. Tests: with the real registry, SYNTHETIC "scientist" transitions generated in the test (clearly labelled synthetic, for example a user who always picks edits that raise TPSA) show the adapted policy beating the base policy on held-out steps; invalid steps are dropped; <5 steps refused; wall-clock cap enforced; job queue limits; adapter fallback when op-id hash differs.
Acceptance: tests green; `python -m studio.adapt.demo` runs the synthetic scientist end to end and prints the evaluation; a screenshot of the adapt panel in your handoff; the two wiring points (server install line, run-config adapter_id) documented. Do not claim real-world gains.
